meetings.title: Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The Council approved buying an already-equipped police truck for up to $80,000. It also passed an emergency City law letting the Mayor appoint Councilmembers to the empty building appeals board, and accepted an $87,100 grant for the Eloy Fire District.
meetings.details:
### What the Council decided
- Routine items approved together included up to $95,000 to equip two new police trucks and an $87,100 Gila River Indian Community grant for the Eloy Fire District (Resolution No. 26-1678) (approved 7-0).
- The Council approved buying a 2024 Ford F-150 police demonstration truck from San Tan Ford for up to $80,000, paid with state marijuana tax money (approved 7-0).
- The truck already has most of its emergency gear and will be used by a community service officer who handles non-criminal reports and takes prisoners to jail.
- A City law change (Ordinance No. 26-1006) lets the Mayor appoint Councilmembers as voting members of the Building Advisory and Board of Appeals (approved 7-0).
- The board cannot meet because it lacks members, and staff expect building code appeals soon.
- The change takes effect right away and is meant to be temporary while the City keeps seeking qualified volunteers.

### Public comments
- A former Maricopa City Councilwoman and Air Force veteran running for office introduced herself and gave the Mayor a challenge coin honoring veterans.

### Announcements
- Sign up at the Community Services building or online for Pizza Palooza (ages 5 to 12, September 18) or a teen painting class (ages 11 to 17, September 25).
- Police will help parents install car seats correctly during National Child Passenger Safety Week, September 20 to 26.
- School fall break starts Thursday, so drivers should watch for children.

meetings.title: Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The Council approved routine items, including fixes to clerical errors in four past resolutions and a new City law letting staff correct such errors. It also heard that the City's investments were worth more than $35 million.
meetings.details:
### What the Council decided
- Routine items approved together fixed clerical errors in four past resolutions, including water and wastewater rate notices (approved 6-0).
- The routine items also included a new City law (Ordinance 26-1005) letting the City Attorney and City Clerk fix clerical errors (approved 6-0).
- The City's investment advisor said City investments were worth more than $35 million on June 30, all in U.S. Treasury bonds (no vote).
- The City earned $359,000 from April through June, and a $203,000 paper loss reflected market swings, not money actually lost.

### Public comments
- No one signed up to speak.

### Announcements
- A free outdoor showing of the movie "Michael" is Saturday, August 29, at 7:30 p.m. at Jones Park.
- Reserve vendor spots online for the community yard sale on Saturday, September 5, 6 a.m. to noon, at Main Street Park.
- Filled sandbags are available at Public Works, 1137 West Houser Road, limit six per household (call 520-466-3082).
